fullPassage:
In high school, everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university, though, everyone seemed much more talented than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt small in comparison. I thought about giving up my dream of becoming an artist. Then one day, I happened to see a drawing I had won an award for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was embarrassed because it wasn't very good. People say you shouldn't compare apples to oranges, and they're right. That's why it doesn't make sense to compare yourself to Internet personalities or even people in your real life. Maybe they had an advantage, or even a disadvantage, that you didn't. If you are going to compare yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is 'yesterday-you.' Only you know where you started and how much effort you've put in. I couldn't see the progress in my ability when I only compared myself to others. Everyone develops differently. I'm able to see now the drawing in the kitchen was full of mistakes that I no longer make. It is empowering to see how I have improved rather than to envy the success of others. Your competition isn't the person next door or the influencer on social media: it's you.

Do you share your opinion in class discussions, or do you just stay silent and keep it to yourself? Like many of you, I often found myself in the second group. A little black hole inside of me swallowed my voice when I considered speaking up. The consequences of being ridiculed or being wrong were always on my mind. Then, after a particularly heated conversation in class, I asked myself, 'What am I afraid of?' I was scared that bad things would happen, but I never thought about good things. When I noticed others taking risks, I knew that I needed to do the same in order to participate. Many people are scared to speak up, but a lot of them do it anyway because they think it's worth it. So I left my comfort zone and started to speak up. I grew intellectually and socially by expressing myself more clearly. I got closer to friends who liked how open I was with them. Now I have more people with whom I can talk, share my ideas, and learn new things. Remember, taking the risk of expressing yourself can be extremely rewarding in unexpected ways.

As I worked through my second year into my third in college, I had more troubles balancing school and personal life. I would get excited, anxious, worried, and bored all at once and then separately. I would get exhausted when I had to write a report for my courses, mediate a disaster between friends, and respond to the comments on my online journal. I was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns, and anxieties, and that was when I read an article with a simple insight. The article advised me to draw two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it: what I eat and drink, how I behave, or what I do after school. The bigger circle is called my circle of concern: things I worry about but have no direct control over. For example, I have no direct control over how my professor will react to my report, but I do have control over the amount of research I do for it. Believing that everything was in my circle of influence left me stressed out and constantly exhausted. By wasting less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to invest more energy into things that mattered.

questions.passage: In high school, everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university, though, everyone seemed much more talented than me, and they all worked __________ I felt small in comparison.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: "너무 열심히 해서 ~하게 느꼈다"라는 so + 부사 + that 구문이 적절하다. hard는 부사이므로 so hard that이 맞다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ so hard that: so + 부사(hard) + that절 = "너무 ~해서 ...하다"
❌ ① so hard: that절이 빠져 뒤의 I felt와 연결 불가
❌ ② such hard: such는 명사 앞에 사용 (such + a/an + 형용사 + 명사)
❌ ④ such hard that: hard가 부사이므로 such 사용 불가
det.tip: so + 형용사/부사 + that ~: 너무 ~해서 ...하다 | such + (a/an) + 형용사 + 명사 + that ~

questions.passage: So I left my comfort zone and started to speak up. I grew intellectually and socially by expressing myself more clearly. I got closer to friends who liked how open I was with them. Now I have more people with __________ I can talk, share my ideas, and learn new things.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 전치사 with 뒤에 오는 목적격 관계대명사이므로 whom이 적절하다. "with whom I can talk" = "내가 이야기할 수 있는 사람들"
det.analysis:
✅ ④ whom: 전치사(with) + 목적격 관계대명사(사람)
❌ ① who: 주격 관계대명사 → 전치사 뒤 불가
❌ ② which: 사물용 관계대명사 → 사람(people) 수식에 부적절
❌ ③ that: 전치사 바로 뒤에 that 사용 불가
det.tip: 전치사 + 관계대명사(사람): with/to/for + whom (전치사 뒤에 who, that 불가)

questions.passage: The bigger circle is called my circle of concern: things I worry about but have no direct control over. For example, I have no direct control over how my professor will react to my report, but I do have control over the amount of research I do for it. __________ that everything was in my circle of influence left me stressed out and constantly exhausted.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 동명사 주어 구문으로 Believing이 적절하다. "모든 것이 내 영향력의 원 안에 있다고 믿는 것이 나를 지치게 했다"
det.analysis:
✅ ① Believing: 동명사 주어 → "~하는 것이" + left(동사)
❌ ② Believed: 과거분사 → 주어 역할 불가
❌ ③ To believe: to부정사 주어 가능하지만, 일반적 사실/습관 서술에는 동명사가 자연스러움
❌ ④ Having believed: 완료 동명사 → 문맥상 시제 앞당김 불필요
det.tip: 동명사 주어: ~ing + 동사 = "~하는 것이 ...하다" (일반적 사실/반복 행위)

questions.passage: Maybe they had an advantage, or even a disadvantage, that you didn't. If you are going to compare yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is 'yesterday-you.' Only you know where you started and how much effort you've put in. I couldn't see the progress in my ability when I only compared myself to others. Everyone develops ①<u>differently</u>. I'm able to see now the drawing in the kitchen was full of mistakes that I ②<u>no more</u> make. It is ③<u>empowering</u> to see how I have improved rather than to envy the success of others.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~③ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② no more → no longer: "더 이상 ~하지 않는다"는 의미로 동사를 수식할 때 no longer를 사용한다. no more는 명사의 양을 수식할 때 사용한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ② no more → no longer: "더 이상 ~하지 않다" = no longer + 동사 (no more는 명사 양 수식)
✅ ① differently: 부사 → 동사 develops를 수식 → 올바름
✅ ③ empowering: 가주어 It ~ to see 구문에서 감정유발 형용사(현재분사) → 올바름
det.tip: no longer vs. no more: no longer + 동사(시간적 "더 이상 ~않다") | no more + 명사(양적 "더 이상의 ~없다")

questions.passage: I would get exhausted when I had to write a report for my courses, mediate a disaster between friends, and respond to the comments on my online journal. I was ①<u>drowning</u> in a sea of responsibilities, concerns, and anxieties, and that was when I read an article with a simple insight. The article advised me ②<u>to draw</u> two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it: ③<u>that</u> I eat and drink, how I behave, or what I do after school.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~③ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ that → what: "내가 먹고 마시는 것"이라는 의미로 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 what이 적절하다. that은 뒤에 불완전한 절이 와야 하지만, 여기서는 eat and drink의 목적어가 필요하므로 what이 맞다.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ that → what: eat and drink의 목적어 역할 + 선행사 포함 = what (that은 명사절 접속사로 완전한 절 필요)
✅ ① drowning: 과거진행 was drowning → "빠져들고 있었다" 올바름
✅ ② to draw: advise + 목적어 + to부정사 → 올바름
det.tip: what vs. that 명사절: what = 선행사 포함(불완전한 절) | that = 접속사(완전한 절)

det.analysis:

questions.passage: Then one day, I happened to see a drawing I had won an award for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was __________ (embarrass) because it wasn't very good.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: embarrass(동사) → embarrassed(형용사): 주어 I(사람)가 "당혹감을 느끼는" 상태이므로 과거분사형 형용사가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
embarrass(동사) → embarrassed(형용사)
I was ______ : 주어가 사람 + 감정을 느끼는 상태 → -ed형
-ed형(embarrassed): 사람이 감정을 느끼는 | -ing형(embarrassing): 감정을 유발하는
det.tip: 감정 분사: 사람 주어 + -ed (embarrassed, excited) | 사물/상황 주어 + -ing (embarrassing, exciting)

det.analysis:
ridicule(동사) → ridiculed(과거분사)
being + p.p. = 수동태 동명사: "~당하는 것"
being ridiculed = 조롱당하는 것
det.tip: being + p.p.: 수동태 동명사 (전치사 of 뒤에 동명사 필요 + 수동 의미)

det.korean: "It is empowering to see how I have improved rather than to envy the success of others" → 자신의 발전을 보는 것이 힘을 주는(empowering)

questions.passage: When I noticed others taking risks, I knew that I needed to do the same in order to participate. Many people are scared to speak up, but a lot of them do it anyway because they think it's worth it. So I left my comfort zone and started to speak up. I grew intellectually and socially by expressing myself more clearly.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 Elias가 자신을 표현하기 위해 벗어난 곳을 본문에서 2단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "So I left my comfort zone and started to speak up" → Elias는 편안한 영역(comfort zone)을 벗어났다.
det.analysis:
left my comfort zone: 편안한 영역을 떠나다 = 새로운 도전을 시작하다
2단어 답 = comfort zone
det.tip: leave one's comfort zone: 익숙한 환경에서 벗어나 도전하다

questions.passage: The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it: what I eat and drink, how I behave, or what I do after school. The bigger circle is called my circle of concern: things I worry about but have no direct control over. For example, I have no direct control over how my professor will react to my report, but I do have control over the amount of research I do for it. Believing that everything was in my circle of influence left me stressed out and constantly exhausted. By wasting less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to invest more energy into things that mattered.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 Abigail이 에너지 낭비를 줄임으로써 중요한 일에 더 투자할 수 있게 된 대상(원)의 이름을 본문에서 3단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "By wasting less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to invest more energy into things that mattered" → 관심의 원에 에너지 낭비를 줄여서 중요한 일에 투자
det.analysis:
circle of concern = 걱정하지만 직접 통제할 수 없는 것들의 영역
에너지 낭비를 줄인 대상 = circle of concern
3단어 답 = circle of concern
det.tip: circle of concern(관심의 원) vs. circle of influence(영향력의 원): 통제 불가 vs. 통제 가능

questions.passage: In high school, everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university, though, everyone seemed much more talented than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt small in comparison. I thought about giving up my dream of becoming an artist.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"Nahyeon dreamed of becoming an illustrator in high school."

det.korean: "In high school, everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I dreamed of becoming an illustrator." → 고등학교에서 삽화가가 되는 꿈을 꾸었다. → True
det.analysis: ✅ True: "dreamed of becoming an illustrator" = 본문과 정확히 일치
det.tip: 시기(in high school)와 내용(dreamed of becoming an illustrator)을 정확히 대조

questions.passage: Do you share your opinion in class discussions, or do you just stay silent and keep it to yourself? Like many of you, I often found myself in the second group. A little black hole inside of me swallowed my voice when I considered speaking up. The consequences of being ridiculed or being wrong were always on my mind. Then, after a particularly heated conversation in class, I asked myself, 'What am I afraid of?' I was scared that bad things would happen, but I never thought about good things.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"Elias always actively shared his opinions in class before the heated conversation."

det.korean: 본문: "I often found myself in the second group" (침묵하는 그룹) → Elias는 격렬한 대화 이전에 적극적으로 의견을 나누지 않았다. "항상 적극적으로 나누었다"는 False.
det.analysis: ❌ False: "I often found myself in the second group" = 침묵하는 쪽 → "always actively shared"와 반대
det.tip: "always actively" vs. "stay silent" → 빈도/태도 부사에 주의
